Lives / Works: Lives and works in London (United Kingdom)
Title: Memorial for Intersections #5
Description: Since 2011, Amalia Pica has been interested in the Venn diagram used to describe group dynamics. These graphic representations were prohibited during the Argentine dictatorship, because they were considered subversive because of their potential ability to think collaborative ways. Coloured geometric shapes in "Memorial for Intersections #5" were manipulated by performers. Here, the artist invents an alternative alphabet as she may have previously been interested in the morse alphabet, radars, flags that remain simple abstract shapes or images for whom no one has the codes.
Materials, supports, techniques: Painted steel and coloured Plexiglas
Acquisition: Purchased at Herald St. Gallery in 2014

Description of the set: "The Line" explores the relationship between reality and fiction. "The substance of time is never linear," she says.

Description:
Dance is central to Marina De Caro. She has been dancing since childhood with her aunt, classic star of the Teatro Colòn of Buenos Aires. For her, creation always begins with questions about body and movement: "How do our eyes travel through images? How do our pores travel through images? What is the relationship between eyes and skin? What is the relationship between eyes, nerves and skin? Colour, drawing, sculpture, knitting respond. Why the body? Because he's political. Freeing the body is freeing perception, making possible other solidarity, other movements, other explorations. Freedom is conquered, too.
Annabelle Gugnon
Materials, supports, techniques: Digital print on blue back to produce and stick to wall
Additional dimensions: Variable dimensions to adapt to space
Acquisition: Purchase at Galerie In Situ / Fabienne Leclerc in 2024

Title:
Hombre-semilla o el mito de lo possible
(Man seed or myth of possible)
Production circumstances: Directed as part of the Biennale d'art contemporain de Lyon 2011
Description: A multicolored, suspended figure at the end of which two exaggeratedly deformed shapes represent both hands.
Materials, supports, techniques: Plaster, wool knitting
Publishable comment:
Gift at the end of the Biennale de Lyon 2011

"Men seeds - metaphors of new men in the midst of rebirth... we need to be reborn in a new form of subjectivity"

Marina De Caro develops her personal poetics between drawing, sculpture and performance. Her works often appear in the form of sculptures that she can wear during performances. They are specially designed to encourage the viewer to experience a shift from daily, to standards that apply to body and serial behavior. The work acquired by the macLYON at the end of the Biennale de Lyon 2015 where it was exhibited gives the metaphor of new men: the seed men. Marina De Caro explains: "Our world needs new beginnings: political, economic, social and emotional. We need the rebirth of a new form of subjectivity. This is the myth of the possible: a new way of seeing things that I believe would allow new utopias, or at least the creation of new possible projects. The seed man is intrinsically involved in his relationship to the natural world. And it's a good (and necessary) starting point. »

Marina De Caro developments her personal poets between drawing, sculpture and performance. Her works are often embossed in the form of sculptures which she wears during performances. These are specially designed to encourage the viewer to experience a shift or break from the everyday, and from the norms that apply to the body and serial behavior. The work acquired by the macLYON following the 2015 Biennale de Lyon, where it was presented, creates the metaphor of a new species of men: ‘seed-men的. Marina De Caro explains: ‘Our world needs new beginnings, whether political, economic, social and emotional. We need the rebirth of a new form of subjectivity. This is the myth of the possible: a new way of seeing things which, I believe, would allow for new utopias, or at least the creation of new possible projects. The seen-man is intrinsically involved in his relationship to the natural world. And this is a good (and necessary) starting point. 

EXPO COLLECTION 2018 macLYON

Title: Isola Bella
Description:
Number of games : 4
For "Isola Bella", Dakic returned to film in Pazaric, near Sarajevo, a boarding school for mentally handicapped children and adolescents founded in 1949, which was intended to be a glory of Yugoslav socialism. The residents who survived the Bosnian war remained forgotten. They're old now, having spent their whole lives confined to this house. Isola Bella is the title of this video, taken from an ancient wallpaper that represents an island of paradise. The artist thus draws inspiration from 19th-century paper-painting motifs to create narratives with marginalized groups.
Materials, supports, techniques: HDV Video
Additional dimensions: Dimensions of the rows of buffered cinema seats

Title:
Hábito/Habitante
(Habit/Habitant)
Description:
Performance / installation to be reactivated.
Martha Araújo carried out her work in the 1980s at the time of the military dictatorship in Brazil (1964-1985). The photographs bear witness to an action of wearing a black dress, attached to the wall, and then trying to get rid of it. Highlighting his commitment to the dictatorial regime, the artist proposes to free everyone's bodies, too long imprisoned. "Hábito/Habitante" is a symbolic gesture embodying a need for freedom.
The dress is a performance work that can be activated by the public.
Materials, supports, techniques: Black fabric, Velcro strips and wooden sticks
Additional dimensions:
Dimensions of wooden sticks: 117cm x 5.5cm x 1.5cm.
CC2022 05/08/2022
Publishable comment: The 49 North 6 East - Frac Lorraine keeps a copy of the dress and has the right to produce it again.

Title: Studying Fertility 3
Production circumstances: Video shot between January and February 2022
Materials, supports, techniques: HD video, color, sound
Publishable comment:
Studying Fertility 3 tells about the research of artist Fabiana Ex-Souza around healing drinks entitled in Brazilian "Garrafadas". Sold at the Ver-O-Peso market in Belém do Pará in the Brazilian Amazon, these preparations made with a mixture of different local plants have been used for generations to cure uterus-related diseases of women. In this quest, Ex-Souza also wonders about the term "care" and practices an intimate poetic about fertility.
This video was produced for the exhibition "Horizones" as part of the artist's nomination in 2022 for the 23rd prize of the Pernod Ricard Foundation.

Title: A Man Called Love
Description: A Man Called Love is a slide projection, accompanied by a soundtrack. This work restores the lived history of Francisco Candido Xavier, a Brazilian medium who devoted his life to notifying the words addressed to him by disembodied minds. Title: Temporal, Aurora e Poente
Description:
Number of games : 41
" The exiled status (which he himself had imposed) has always obsessed Hercule Florence, moving away from his homeland but allowing him to consider nature as he could never have seen it in Europe. That's why the skies he chooses to paint are so special and reflect a taste for the mysterious. The fact that they are so remarkable justifies that there may be defects in their representation. Hercules Florence accepted its own limits and the impossibility of fixing these fleeting moments and the inevitable variations of light and colors. These studies are therefore inevitably incomplete. Studies of Heaven for the use of young landscapers is a compilation of drawings of extraordinary skies offered to painters who would succeed him, which would allow to build a complete image. Like the inventions he wanted to publish, this Atlas had to be able to be used by others elsewhere, and perhaps at another time. He added to each scene depicted a detailed description, indicating how to correct or improve his vision through both humble and ambitious instructions.

And here I am, 180 years after the creation of the Teatro Celeste in Florence, not completely observing its detailed instructions but nevertheless taking its studies from heaven as the basis for new works. Just as attracted by the changes of lights and the fusion of colors visible in the sky, I extracted colors from some of his drawings – aurora, stormy skies, sunset clouds – to create gradient palettes. Faithful to this announced failure of the possibility of recreating the atmosphere of a moment, unable to reproduce a correct sky, and not even trying to make an image of it, I reduced the sky to transitions of colors crossed by light. They are printed on fabric, exploring an effect that Hercules Florence would have liked, although different from her "transparent paintings". Temporal, Aurora and Poente became curtains dividing space, layers superimposing to bring a variation in density and color effects.

All the works I made using gradients of printed colours were originally the need to describe the transition from the bright blue horizon to the dark grey of the polluted days of winter in São Paulo, dirty, dry and heavy. For years I have experienced many ways of printing until getting the material ability to create a resemblance to this visual experience. It finally happened when the translucent canvas was found to be backlit by the natural light that crossed the frame of the ink points, as on particles suspended in the air. This created a complete space and organized with the horizon, evoking a landscape without being sufficiently figurative to be perceived as an image; and too many shades do not make it monochrome or pure abstraction. Since then, I have created many color gradients printed on surfaces intended to be installed on an architecture. It is only when I place them somewhere, in relation to a given space and time, that a (new) narrative appears thanks to the interaction created with the body of the viewer. (Lucia Koch)
Materials, supports, techniques: Silk muslin curtain made up of 41 shades of 3 different gradients, suspended from rails fixed to the ceiling by pressures.

With Espetáculo, Ana Mazzei explores a new territory of actions, in which objects are placed in an ambiguous position, as if they were the main characters of a theatre without action, or the public of an act that takes place in the body of the visitor. Title: Colônia
Production circumstances:
Colônia is part of a series of sculptures that deal with geometry and its variations.
The work was produced for a collective exhibition at the House of Egorn gallery in March 2018 in Berlin
Description:
Installation consisting of 7 wooden and metal sculptures.
Ana Mazzei develops a multidisciplinary practice that explores the structures, materiality and history of representation, often in connection with the distinction between theatre and reality in contemporary life. It creates a unique visual vocabulary combining wooden orthogonal sculptures with organic or figurative forms, influenced by late modernist movements in Brazil. His constructions use theatrical procedures, with objects as accessories to suggest an unknown ritual ceremony, engaging the spectator as an interpreter.
Materials, supports, techniques: Wood, fabric, metal and painted wood
Acquisition: Buy at Emmanuel Hervé Gallery in 2019

Title: VOSTOK
Production circumstances: VOSTOK
Description:
Leticia Ramos carries out a vast research work within which she designs fictions that branch and formalize in her photographs, films and installations. His works are part of devices for capturing and reconstructing urban or natural environments. With a particular interest in science fiction, the dark areas of the globe studied by man and laws that regulate the universe, she works to mix the scientist with the imagination, the documentary with fiction in complex "geographical narratives". The atmospheres resulting from the series ERBF, Bitácora or VOSTOK refer to the mysterious explorations of scientific novels.
VOSTOK is inspired by a Russian research base located in Antarctica above the underwater lake of the same name. Extracts from the previous glaciation were extracted from this base of drilling at about 4 km depth. In 2012, in residence in PIVô in Sao Paulo, the artist designs and shows an artificial decor from a projection screen, a small pool, an aquarium and a submarine model. The soundtrack comes from a performance performed in collaboration with artist Lùcia Koch and composer and conductor Rossano Snel. The project finally brings together an artist's book, a vinyl record and a film. The audio-visual version presented in the Video Room offers a fictional trip to this prehistoric lake and evokes landscapes submerged in the depths, as lost in time.
Materials, supports, techniques:
Stone: basalt
Bricks, water; yellow filter, fishing wire
Unique
Reference: OSRAM universal 20 W LUZ DO DIA ESPECIAL Brasil K528 length 60.5 (with metal nipples) diameter 2.5 cm

Title: Ceu
Description:
Number of games : 4
Number of objects : 10
Around 1827, in his travel diary entitled Viagem Fluvial do Tietê ao Amazonas, Hercules Florence describes the Chapada Diamantina, a region of steep rock formations, near Mount São Jeronimo. After a rough climb into the waterfalls on the mountainside, he takes the time to observe and draw this extraordinary landscape. It may be the most magical moment of his journey. The short film The Blue Night by Leticia Ramos reconstructs the starry vault, the race of clouds and the shadows above the typical rocks of the Chapada Diamantina. Inspired by "transparent paintings" and stereoscopy, it evokes an imaginary night, lost in the distance of time and space. The film was made in stop-motion and with the processes specific to the microfilm that is still in use in Brazil to copy and keep official documents. The decor consists of many strata and small models photographed on a classic shooting table. The soundtrack combines nocturnal bird songs and recordings of sound environments characteristic of this fascinating region. The soundtrack was recorded during a live studio session with an electronic instrument, the theremin, and an analog synthesizer for the orchestra. Leticia Ramos proposes to donate this film to the NMNM, which produced it for the exhibition "Hercules Florence. The new Robinson." On the occasion of this exhibition, an entire room of Villa Paloma was also dedicated to a beautiful series of skys from Hercules Florence. During the process of research for the exhibition and creation of the film The Blue night, Leticia Ramos is inspired and created a series of ten photograms entitled Sky. The acquisition of this series would give a good context to Leticia Ramos' participation in the exhibition and acquisition of The Blue night. These unique pieces, of incredible materiality, have never been shown before.
Materials, supports, techniques: Silver N&B: photogram on photographic paper Ilford art 300 (type to define matte texture) developed in an Ilford teller, fixed in a fast fixer and turned to selenium

Collection: Institut d'art contemporain, Collection Frac Rhône-Alpes
Title: Untitled
Production circumstances: Multiple made in 7 copies + 3 artist events, in February 2018, and produced by Friends of the IAC, Villeurbanne/Rhône-Alpes.
Materials, supports, techniques: Mosaic, Venetian enamel on plywood, plastic
Registration: S.D.B.DR.: in black ink: Maria Thereza Alvas Jimmie Durham 18
Publishable comment:
The multiples are miniatures of Mediterranean, the great mosaic present in the first room of the exhibition of Maria Thereza Alves & Jimmie Durham,The Middle Earth (IAC - 2018) For artists, this is not a serial work but a work of publishing. They were designed in the same energy as exposure: with four hands, in a short temporality, by the principle of assembly of collected objects, with a drolatic aspect.
These small mosaics are made in a traditional fashion inherited from Roman Antiquity, with Venetian enamel. However, the freedom of expression of both artists is revealed by the irregular edges and reliefs of their creations. The light is reflected in these asperities and animates the surface of each multiple of different effects.
Similarly, the square shape does not offer any real meaning of reading. The miniatures evoke a landscape on top where the blue of the sky and the blue of the sea merge to weave a bundle of relationships between the elements. Diversified and unexpected, the latter give mosaics a multicultural and transhistoric dimension: fragments of dishes (cup, plate), gems, stones, pearls, electronic components, personalization accessory (death heads). Far from its usual codes and models, each detail participates in the active dialogue on the Métis heritage of Middle Earth.
Acquisition: Gift from Friends of the Institute of Contemporary Art, Villeurbanne/Rhône-Alpes in 2019

Title: Pentimenti
Description: The starting point is a picture: the equestrian portrait of Philip IV by Velasquez. The film deepens the relationship between the dressage of a horse and the construction of an image. A trained horse, mounted by an anonymous rider, travels the space with insistence. Remote in the background, it appears and disappears on the edges of the frame to appear close again.
Materials, supports, techniques: DVD

Title: Vaso de Leche
Subtitle: Bogota
Collaborators: Printing, 2010
Description:
The action "Vaso de Leche, Bogota", 1979 is one of the actions carried out at the invitation of the Chilean CADA group to participate in an operation "para No Morir de Hambre en el Arte" (To not starve in art).
Cecilia Vicuna was inspired by a scandal that at the same time killed 1920 children by the sale of damaged milk. In order to denounce this collective poisoning, Vicuna announced that she was going to spill a glass of milk into the street and people joined her to attend this performance.
Materials, supports, techniques: Digital print on Epson paper.

Title: What is Para Ud. la Poesia?
Description: In March 1980, Cecilia Vicuna traveled the city of Bogota, questioning mendians, prostitutes and police officers about what they thought poetry was. People improvised their answers thus revealing the richness of the oral tradition of the city. Filmed in 16 mm, digitized and transferred on video in New York.
Materials, supports, techniques: Video, color, sound.

Title: Party if Pasión
Subtitle: New York
Collaborators: Print Artist's Protocol, 2010
Description: Created on the west highway of Manhattan "Parti si Pasión, New York", 1981 is one of Vicuña's contributions to the Chilean CADA group following an invitation for Operation "Ay Sudamérica". As a poet and plastician, Cecilia Vicuña created the word "participation" using the full potential of its meaning: saying yes to passion is taking part in suffering. It was painted in the colours of the American flag on the road leading to the WTC, today Ground Zero.
Materials, supports, techniques: Digital print on Epson paper.

Title: Quipu Austral
Description:
Installation in situ.
The installation consists of unwoven wool ribbons falling from the ceiling to the ground. Wool ribbons are of specific colours. The wool used for FRAC is partly that produced in Tasmania for the Sydney Biennale and partly produced by Bergère de France. A sound piece accompanies the installation.
Materials, supports, techniques: Non-woven wool ribbons and bran
Additional dimensions:
Variable dimensions. Minimum 60m2.
Dimensions of all wool pellets assembled: h. 80 x W. 76 x W. 76 cm

Description of the set: "Another look at the insignificant" is an autobiographical series, it includes 25 photographs and 25 texts dated from 1982 to 2014. The photographs present the facades of the various places where Ingrid Wildi Merino has worked since his emigration to Switzerland with his family. The texts describe the different jobs she has exercised in these places and show the joint evolution of her mastery of the language and architecture surrounding it.

Title: Haze and Fog
Description: His latest film Haze and Fog (Brume and Fog), 2013, testifies to the uneasiness of living in a large Chinese city like Beijing, with a society invaded by the video game industry and the overtaking consumption symbolized for the artist by this thick fog. It features characters (employees, a prostitute, a pregnant woman, a disabled person...) who seem to have no pleasure in living, applying only to a certain routine and gestures more or less controlled. The artist invents a parallel universe with zombies who could fully live their desires and emotions, without being locked in binding settings like the living. Inspired by popular shows and games such as The Walking Dead or Silent Hill, Cao Fei says "observe zombies", "these prophets of misfortune", before the apocalypse, which, in his imagination, are nothing disturbing but rather resemble " fragments of "light," as if there were a momentary revival of consciousness before death (...)" (cit. Cao Fei in an explanatory text of the work entitled "H Haze and Fog").
Materials, supports, techniques: HD video, color, sound
Acquisition: Gift of the International Circle of the Friends of the National Museum of Modern Art, 2014

Lives / Works: Lives and works in Vanves (Hautes-de-Seine, France)
Title: Titanium Museum #4
Production circumstances: Draw made as part of the photographic control Breathings
Place of production: taken in front of the Renée Gailhoustet ensemble in Saint-Denis
Description:
The framework of Breathings and the accompaniment of La Capsule allowed
the artist to discover many sites witnesses of modernist architecture
present on the department and thus prolong its work on the meaning
the concept of modernity. His meeting with the agents of the Heritage Office
contemporary has been essential for, she says, "to emerge from the clichés backed by
cities for a fairer and more accurate approach." His photographs
want to set a framework, invite the viewers to let their imagination go
and thus trigger a story, a fictional narrative unique to each.
It does not attempt to document strictly speaking, but rather to provoke
dream from known architectural elements. His discreet interventions
: stitches, felt bonding, have the ambition to disturb the
and introduce a potential fiction.
The titles of the photographs reflect the difference between its
works and the real. "Titanium" comes from a dream where she finds herself in
a mysterious museum, the Titanium museum composed of a succession of
independent cubes in which the dreamer walks.
The three photographs proposed are attached to architectural places
emblematic of the department: a factory witnessing pre-industrial activities
and two architectural ensembles signed by reference architects
modern and post modern, namely Renée Gailhoustet in Saint-Denis and Ricardo
Bofill in Noisy-le-Grand.
Materials, supports, techniques: Lambda color print, embroidery and felt, framed under glass

Title: One Thousand and One Attempts to Be an Ocean
Collaborators: Producer: Le Fresnoy, national studio of contemporary arts, Tourcoing (France)
Description: One Thousand and One Attempts to Be an Ocean corresponds above all to a rhythm, a hypnotic resonance that overflows the images of their content to become sensation and energy. It consists of micro events coming from the so-called "satisfying video" category that pull on the internet. Without beginning or ending, the abstract narrative develops on the mode of borrowing by referring to both trance and minimal music. The images embody until exhaustion this desire for a bottomless wave, expression of an artificial oceanic feeling mixed with the entropy of our information societies.
Materials, supports, techniques: Video, color, sound

Title: Comfortable shoes
Description: In Uncomfortable shoes, hundreds of black and coloured ballerinas dance on the walls and let appear aerially, almost anamorphic the sentence: "They have gone away; Yet they have nowhere to go." These arabesques of shoes that seem to escape from the ground evoke above all contemporary migratory flows. The work consists of 100 to 150 shoes (depending on the size of the space) fixed to the wall, of two kinds: coloured (named "three-inch goldenly" in imperial China) and black (unitarist shoes of Maoist China). The preserved set consists of 373 coloured shoes and 307 black shoes.
Materials, supports, techniques: installation of plain black cotton shoes
Acquisition: Purchase at Galerie Kamel Mennour in 2021

Lives / Works: Lives and works in Taipei (China, Taiwan) and Paris (France)
Title: Planet Tree Mantra
Production circumstances: First performance at FIAC in the Jardin des Plantes in Paris.
Description: During an in situ intervention, Charwei Tsai calligraphie sutra du coeur, a fundamental Buddhist text, on the trunk of a historic and emblematic tree of the Jardin des Plantes: the plane tree of the Orient, planted in 1785 by Buffon. The heart sutra, which the artist learned by heart during his childhood in Taiwan, is a pillar of Buddhist wisdom, evoking the evanescence of everything. It is in Chinese calligraphic characters that Charwei Tsai writes these words on the trunk of Buffon's plane tree. The public is invited to attend the writing process, and to observe the long and applied gesture of calligraphy, symbolizing the encounter between the memory of a person, that of a millennium thought, and that of a tree more than two centuries old.
Materials, supports, techniques: Performance

During an in situ intervention, Charwei Tsai calligraphie sutra du coeur, a fundamental Buddhist text, on the trunk of a historic and emblematic tree of the Jardin des Plantes: the plane tree of the Orient, planted in 1785 by Buffon. The heart sutra, which the artist learned by heart during his childhood in Taiwan, is a pillar of Buddhist wisdom, evoking the evanescence of everything. It is in Chinese calligraphic characters that Charwei Tsai writes these words on the trunk of Buffon's plane tree. The public is invited to attend the writing process, and to observe the long and applied gesture of calligraphy, symbolizing the encounter between the memory of a person, that of a millennium thought, and that of a tree more than two centuries old.
Materials, supports, techniques: Digital print on paper.

Title: We Came Whirling Out of Nothingness
Series title: We Came Whirling Out of Nothingness
Description: We Came Whirling Out of Nothingness is a series of watercolour drawings on rice paper, representing different forms of spirals on which also appears the Heart Sutra. The Chinese calligraphy she uses for this work allows her to write both vertically and horizontally. The text itself is designed to generate a dynamic movement, gradually dispersing the texts, through their repetition, to the outside of the paper until they reach nothingness. The visitor is invited to be lost in contemplation of the essence of the void whose circle is the symbol par excellence, embodying the cyclical idea of life.
Materials, supports, techniques: Ink and watercolour on rice paper

In 2002, a group of scientists began tracking the movements of a species of local deer, elaph deer, who live in the area formerly occupied by the Iron Curtain, between Germany and the Czech Republic.
They found that the daily journeys of the cervids are still influenced by the ghostly presence of the curtain: on either side of the border, hordes of deer move as if the barrier still existed.

HD video, color, sound

Description: "The black sun of the title evokes as much the solar eclipse as this "black bile" to which the ancient doctors attributed the melancholic and suicidal impulses whose artists were going to suffer especially and who invade here the existence of Antonia, a lyric singer whose dark beauty illuminates the film. Laura presents, in a pudic and elliptical staging, several facets of the character of Antonia. The delicately explored family ties are not so much in search of the origin of evil as a form of introspection with several voices: those of the aunt, the mother and the daughter - the director herself, who through fiction seeks to get rid of family destiny." Céline Guénot, Catalogue FID Marseille 2016

Description of the set:
Nora Turato's books are the basis of her entire artistic process, which includes the creation of a book, the making of material works (wallpaintings, poster, sculpture...), the performances from which the texts are drawn from the book, and then the recording of the video.

Nora Turato collects words and phrases from various sources: internet, media titles, advertisements, conversations, books, commercial products, and her own thoughts. His Pool #1, #2, #3 assemble and arrange these texts into a growing script that the artist memorizes and interprets, alternating rhythm and tone, voices and modes. In its virtuoso performances, speech, graphics and books intertwine to explore the possibilities of language in an oversaturated culture of information. The accompanying publication, which accompanies the artist throughout his development, serves simultaneously as an accessory, decor, exhibition, archive and artist's book.

Title: Harvesting
Production circumstances: 1% artistic
Collaborators:
Owner: Conseil départemental de la Seine-Saint-Denis, Bobigny (France)
Owner: Fayat, Bordeaux (France)
Description:
The images installed by Estefanía Peñafiel Loaiza, artist of Ecuadorian origin, in Barbara College in Stains are the fruit of a harvest carried out with a group of students. The artist conducted a video workshop to create moving images related to different meanings of the word "culture". The word of course means the transmission of knowledge, the very principle of teaching. But it also refers to cultivating, sowing and thus to the gardening past of the neighborhood where the college was built. Finally, synonymous with "civilization", and understood as all the influences suffered by an individual in his or her life (family, history, language, geographical traditions), "culture(s)" recall the mixedness and different origins of the students.
The students filmed their passages in and around the building, promoting a dialogue between inside and outside. From these rushes, the artist made a selection of images to be implanted in the interstitial spaces of the college. Printed on curtains, windows, computer screens, or on the canteen card, the selected images appear subtly depending on the natural light, the position of the person looking at them and the attention they have. A database of selected images is available to the college for other uses, such as a reserve of images for the future.
Materials, supports, techniques:
Images on different facilities
- wallpapers for college computers
- illustrations / iconography college website
- images distributed / printed on the canteen map
- images distributed / printed on stationery and official college documents
- image(s) printed on curtains or blinds in several building spaces
- image(s) in large format on windows
- image(s) glued to the counter-steps
Additional dimensions: images scattered in different areas of the college

Title: Dyslexia 3
Materials, supports, techniques: Diptych: acrylic and ballpoint pen on Iranian world maps printed on paper
Registration: B.G.S.D.R.T.: Signed and dated on the bottom map, in the white margin on the lower left edge: "Ghazel, August 2015". Titled on the back of both cards: "Dyslexia 3".

Title: Dyslexia
Description:
In the artist's words: The world maps are a symbol of my ‘in transit' state since I left Iran in 1986.
In the series of drawings on the real maps of the world: Black tide and Dyslexia, j'unify the borders and I erase the lands...
There are no more borders, no more flags, no more countries. I want to show the conflicts, disasters, corruption and pollution caused by man
Materials, supports, techniques:
Installation of 4 framed painted maps
Acrylic and ballpoint pen on world map printed on icy paper
Additional dimensions: 2 painted maps : 140 x 100 cm and 100 x 70 cm

Title:
The Shadow Under The Web
(The shadow under the veil)
Collaborators: Mario Chiodi, José Santamaria
Description:
Installation of four video sound projections simultaneously projected on the four walls of a room (video tapes slow down in loop). The room or construction for the installation must be about 10x10 meters, ceiling height 305 to 366 cm high.
Depending on the type of headlamp, it is possible to install them in the centre of the ceiling (Zenith CRT Type) or on the walls on the highest parts (Sony LCD Type)
A woman dressed in a black chador runs tirelessly through deserted markets and streets, patios and mosques. Between the public and the private, the secular and the religious, the history and the present, it goes beyond every space where the Muslim woman negotiates her own presence, without fighting against the codes of individual behavior, to maintain a prescribed balance of society.
Concept: Shirin Neshat
Direction: Mario Chiodi
Cameraman: José Santamaria
Laser disk number 1 : mosque
Laser disk number 2 : walls of the city
Laser disc #3: streets
Laser disk #4 : market
Materials, supports, techniques: 4 simultaneous sound colour video projections / DVD

Description:
Photography and Persian Writing:
English translation of Persian in cat. "Shirin Neshat", Marco Noire Editore, Torino, 1997:

Face to Face with God
Poem by Forough Farokhzad

From the prison confines of darkness
From the turbid cespool of the world
Hear my needful clamor,
O, one God.

Give this watch of blackness, and
Perhaps you'll see within my breast
The source and substance
Of sin and corruption

The heart you gave me, it isn't a heart
Beating in blood; free it, gold
Keep it empty of carnal desires,
Or encumber it with affection and fidelity

Only you already and only you know
The secrets of that first sin;
Only you are capable of earning
To my soul the original Bliss.

Give me a love that will shape me
Like the angels in your heaven,
Give me a friend, a lover in whom I might see
A glimpse of the bliss of your being.


Face to Face with God
Forough Farokhzad Poem

Prison Limits of Darkness
The world's turbid cloaque
Hear my cry,
O you who can so much, one God.

Destroy this veil of darkness, and
Maybe you'll see inside my chest
Source and substance
Sin and corruption

The heart you gave me is not a heart
Beating by blood; release him, or
Keep it from fleshly desires
Or drink it of tenderness and fidelity

Only you are conscious and you only know
The secrets of this first sin;
Only you can agree
To my soul the original Beatitude.

Give me a love that will shape me
Like the angels of your paradise
Give me a friend, a lover in whom I can
To see the bliss of your being.

Translated from English to French by the Institut d'Art Contemporain de Villeurbanne, 2005

Forough Farokhzad (1935-1967) is an Iranian poet

Description of the set:
This set is the result of the performance "Oscillation" created in 2014 at the Etemad gallery in Teheran. The performance itself is part of a series of works produced under the theme of Instable Balance.
The performance, which gave birth to sculpture and video, was perpetuated for eight consecutive days, five hours each day. During these eight days, sets of dishes were cleaned and arranged in a wardrobe, which was regularly thrown down. Debris of dishes were redisposed according to the extent of their breakage, inside the installation or on a tray presented as a work of art. These trays later became sculptures, in boxes of plexiglas in particular.

Lives / Works: Lives and works in Beirut, Lebanon and Paris (France)
Title: Portrait of a Lake
Production circumstances:
A first version of the smaller paper work, showing the map of a river and not a lake, was produced and shown at the Akinci gallery in Amsterdam in 2017.
A second verison of the work was commissioned and exhibited at the Sharjah Biennial entitled "Tamawuy" in 2017. This version made the cover of Art Press 444 dedicated to the Biennale. This version of the work is identical to that acquired by the Frac Franche-Comté.
The version of the Frac Franche-Comté was produced by the Musée des Abattoirs de Toulouse in preparation for the collective exhibition "Go! Go!" held at the Espace d'art contemporain de Bédarieux in 2019.
Collaborators: Printer and designer
Description:
"Portrait of a lake" consists of a suspended map. We see above us the contours of a lake and its surroundings. This representation, dating back to 1938, wets as it moves and is "reactivated". The water that crosses it becomes lake water; The water drops that flow from the water form a puddle that redraws the contours of the lake. A self-portrait drawn by the lake, with its own material. The lake in question is the lake of Yamamonne – of the Ugaritic "yam": small sea. On its east bank lie the remains of a Roman sanctuary. Formerly dedicated to Asarté-Vénus, goddess of fertility, the sanctuary also housed statues of the god-pattres, protectors of agriculture and pastoral life. Built not far from the "Source of the Forty Martyrs", the main irrigator of the lake, the sanctuary was in direct connection with water and associated purification rites. Abundant in water in the spring, after melting snow, the lake gradually emptied until the end of summer. Overtaking the Bekaa valley, which it partly irrigates, its water also irrigates the illegal crops of Haschisch from the village of Yamamonne. Located on the geological fault of the Levant, which separates east from the Mediterranean from the Arabic plate, Lake Yammuné is a "sweep-apart", a vacuum resulting from the sliding of the two tectonic plates. Starting from Jordan, the fault crosses Lebanese geography in its entirety, as well as Palestine, Israel and Syria, before ending in Turkey, and is responsible for a significant number of earthquakes in the Middle East. Close to the nature of the lake, its cycles and its history, the work also evokes in its form a veil, a tent, a breast... The hemp map suspended above the visitors represents part of Lebanon. The fabric is impermeabilized on the back, except for a portion in the centre, corresponding to Lake Yammuné. Every day, water is poured into the formed curve, passing through the map and flowing on the floor of the exhibition room. A puddle then forms, drawing the contours of a "new lake", echoing the mapping but also the real lake. The room indeed makes several references to the specifics of this lake. During snowmelt, the lake is abundant but gradually empties until the end of summer. The fact of pouring water daily reminds us of this particular feature. Similarly, the puddle evaporates and disappears until a new puddle reappears. Finally, this work proposes geopolitical reflection. Lake Yammuné is located on the geological fault of the Levant, which leaves Jordan, crosses all Lebanon as well as Palestine, Israel, Syria and Turkey. It is responsible for many seismic events in the Middle East. We can then think that the work echoes the political upheavals of the region. The fabric drawn by the four strings also symbolizes this tension and recalls the tectonic plates, responsible for geological movements. Stéphanie Saadé paints a picture of a lake that has disappeared, on the fault of the Levant, whose waters dried up when they were diverted to irrigate the region. Water flows from the ceiling in a hanging canvas on which is printed a map of 1938; and the circles drawn by these drops on the ground evoke the ghostly form of this lake."
Anaël Pigeat, Art Press n°444, May 2017
Materials, supports, techniques: Installation: printing on cotton canvas partially impermeabilized on the back, hemp ropes, water poured daily during activation of the work
Additional dimensions: Dimensions of the canvas: 200 x 300 cm
Acquisition: Purchase at Galerie Anne Barrault in 2024

Title: Untitled (11 March 2005)
Description: The issue of engagement is addressed in the video Untitled (11 March 2005), which consists of a long sequence plan on a rue de Paris before, during and after a demonstration. The usual protagonists (order service, politicians, demonstrators, police...) appear on the screen until the arrival of the sweepers and cleaning services of the city, which systematically erase the traces of the event, until the next demonstration, in an endless movement. Between registration and erasure, this cycle seems never to have to fulfill this desire and expectation of change born from the last major collective protest movement in the late 1960s. However, this space left vacant may at any time be appropriate and occupied by all.

Title: Stoning
Description:
The work of Latifa Echakhch is proof that art can be conducive to exchange and socially engaged without being condescending. While the sculptures she makes are particularly subtle and delicate, the visitor should not be deceived by this discreet sensitivity when the artist questions vast subjects such as culture, geography and personal or collective history. She explores these notions through everyday objects, images and situations and places them at the heart of social and political debate. The understanding of his works is not immediate, but it becomes obvious if he decides to delay it. However, looking at them deeper inevitably leads to a question about the certainties that they seemed to promise in the beginning.

The conceptual and visual strength of this combination of minimalism and romanticism is misleading, and what is imposed is a fundamental belief in the dignity of subjects and of what art can bring as fields of reflection, even when it is the most severe and critical. Ordinary objects thus become testimonies of feelings such as melancholy or anger and offer a silent view of the bankruptcy of utopias.

Stoning (2010), work produced for Latifa Echackch's exhibition at FRAC Champagne-Ardenne (April 2 to May 23, 2010), entitled A reminder of birds, is a constellation of carved stones that evokes both the Stoning the Refrigerator (1996) by Jimmie Durham and the works of Land Art of the 1970s, but also finds a resonance in the most burning news. Exposure The bird recall was organised in partnership with the GAMeC – Galleria d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea de Bergamo in Italy.
Materials, supports, techniques: Stones
Acquisition: Purchase at Kamel Mennour Gallery in 2010

Description:

Here is a game with the top and bottom, the front and the back. Title: Landscape (Moses)
Description:
Number of objects : 11
Latifa Echakhch, the mechanical garden
NMNM - Villa Sauber
20.04 - 31.10.2018

Invited by the NMNM to design an exhibition for the Villa Sauber before its closure for work, Latifa Echakhch designed an installation inspired by the tradition of the romantic landscape, characterized by the representations of a breathtaking nature and a ruined architecture. The mechanical garden combines the distant memories of Monte Carlo's invention – from the creation of the Opéra Garnier to the lush gardens of exotic plants – with the impressions and childhood memories of the artist.
Composed on the scale of a villa, it involves our perception of space and time, indicating the possibility of a survival of nature in a post-apocalyptic decor.

Forty plywood panels cut and painted with landscape or architectural motifs are scattered in the museum's black rooms – related for the occasion behind the scenes of a theatre. They were made from the paper models of Alphonse Visconti, who was the designer of the Monte Carlo Opera between 1903 and 1924.
Latifa Echakhch has selected fragments of models for heteroclite productions such as Pompeii, Moses, Helen in Egypt, Jerusalem, and Masks and Bergamasques, created in Monaco in 1919 in the spirit of Verlaine's Galante Festivals. The selected details were then produced in the form of decorations and then deployed in the exhibition space, freely recomposing a landscape as fake as it was fantasized. This installation, which shows upside down the decor as well as its smallest painted details, annihilates the illusionist function of painting as well as its narrative character, to plunge visitors into the heart of an uncertain environment.

Title: Automate series
Description: The automatons of Galéa's collection were presented at Villa Sauber for almost forty years. Despite changes in costumes and old restorations that are sometimes unscrupulous, they are still mostly in working order. By filming the original automatons in front of the electric replicas made by a master watchmaker for the former National Museum of Monaco, Latifa Echakhch repeats the feeling of "disturbing strangeness" related to these anthropomorphic sculptures, and places in abyss through the screen, through fugitive planes, the mirror game between the automaton and its double, the original and its copy.
Materials, supports, techniques: 5 colour and sound videos

Description of the set:
"Diwana (Customs) brings together a set of plans showing the daily journeys drawn by smugglers from the city of Ceuta. Each journey, made several times in the week or even in the day, is drawn on paper by the carriers and carriers of goods, then translated into blueprint prints (literally "blue print" obtained by the cyanotypy).
By choosing this process, Randa Maroufi gives a certain nobility and special value to these men and women, whom they hardly know in the landscape of their daily lives.
The Diwana series allows to resonate the lines of the informal urban system set up by smugglers
with more conventional architects and planners."

Publishable comment:
SYNOPSIS
In the Intruders series, women "intruders" occupy the time of a public space staging. They take the same gestures, the same postures as men in such places: they play cards, watch a football match in the indifference of the flow of time. They occupy the terraces, put themselves in display in the strangeness of a public space of exclusion, that of gender.

Title: Bodywork, Lycée Pro from the Intrudes series
Production circumstances: Draws produced as part of the photographic control Breathings
Description:
For several years, Randa Maroufi has been conducting an investigation into the position of women in public space through the project "The Intruders". After having taken an interest in "the street"Belgium and then in Paris in the golden gout district, she wanted to settle in a high school to seize the genrée distribution within the training course. The context of Breathing allowed him to realize this idea involving two high schools in Seine-Saint-Denis thanks to the accompanied by the Maison Populaire de Montreuil.

This series is part of a photographic and installation work that builds images related to social phenomena such as border crossing, or customs officials' gestures. She replays specific situations to image them by working with extras and non-professionals. These photographic stagings put emotion at a distance, and subjects shared. In doing so, they invite discussion and exchange.

The artist states: "Public space is an area of democracy, plurality of discourses and usages[ ...] The territory - like the people - bears witness to a history, a cultural and social identity. At first glance, it is mixed, but the imbalances between the two sexes remain deep.... »

By immersing high school girls from Montreuil d'Aubervilliers, in the body class of the Jean-Pierre Timbaud vocational high school, the artist shares a new look at the familiar stages of learning in the automotive fields operated usually by men and but here embodied by women. Randa Maroufi worked about twenty hours with the students, on the basis of volunteerism, to explain and make want to participate in this work, and then to stage, in the most realistic way possible, the professional gestures related to the bodywork.

The three images were produced in cinematographic conditions where each gesture was checked by future professionals; stop on image of a ghost film, these images were displayed on the city walls during the summer of 2022. They are produced in the form of framed photographs to enter the collection and thus be exhibited in different contexts. They are presented at the Biennale de Lyon in 2022 with other works from the series Les Intruses.
Materials, supports, techniques:
Colour photography, fine art collage print Dibond,
framed frame aluminium plexi optium museum

Title: The politicians are saying (Los políticos están dicindo)
Description: This sculpture is inspired by a story that the artist has read about the clepsydra that, in the past, was used to measure the length of the discourse of kings. The people, who could not listen to this speech, could know that the king spoke when they saw this water flowing. Tania Pérez Córdova is thus inspired by stories that she gleans on a daily basis and that she remembers as abstract stories whose context does not matter. For The politicians are saying (Los políticos están diciendo), the artist has reproduced in aluminum cast two plastic buckets that can be seen in the streets of Mexico City. The artificial saliva that is contained in the highest bucket flows through the other bucket through a tap whose drip lasts about twenty minutes, the daily speech of the Mexican President. This artificial saliva is a mixture obtained from oral sprays that can be sold to people who make speeches. Tania Pérez Córdova is interested in materials that are replicas of body fluids, extensions of the human body. Thus this sculpture becomes the receptacle of all the speeches that we produce and that surround us. The artist also includes a part of chance in his works, regularly carried out in collaboration with artisans. It retained the unexpected shape of the bucket placed on the ground, obtained during the melting of aluminum in its mould.
Materials, supports, techniques: 2 elements in aluminum cast iron, water, artificial saliva, plastic irrigation system.
Additional dimensions:
In exhibition
Variable dimensions. H 74 x W 80 x D 64 cm
Duration: about 20 minutes, duration of the daily speech of the Mexican President
Element of cast aluminium n°1 : H 24,1 cm x Diameter 29,6 cm
Aluminium cast iron element n°2 : H 23,8 cm x W 33 cm x D 31 cm
Base: H 50 cm x W 80 cm x D 30 cm

Title: Ethnica I
Collaborators: Framer Simon Beaugié pictures frames ltd
Description: Gathering images from archives and magazines, the Nigerian artist offers a reflection on his experience as an African woman in a world that has experienced slavery and colonization. The way she looks at herself is influenced by the idea that other people and the media are making themselves and black women in general. The technique of collage allows him to juxtapose these disparate identities and to create hybrid self-portraits.
Materials, supports, techniques: Collage on Arches watercolor paper.
Acquisition: Purchased at Purdy Hicks Gallery in 2015

Description of the set:
Nightsea Crossing is a performance performed twenty-two times (in the form of "sittings"), for one or several days (minimum one day, maximum sixteen days), all over the planet (Sydney, Ushimado, Chicago or Kassel), during which Marina Abramovic and Ulay sit face to face in the presence of the public, immobile and imperturbably silent, in a meditative posture of extreme attention.

It was at the end of this unique performance that the Museum invited the two artists, and it was in Lyon in 1986, after a six-year journey that led them to all continents, that they finally finished Nightsea Crossing: on October 9 and 10.

The Museum proposes to the two artists to design simultaneously the last two days of performance, perfectly circumscribed in time and destined to disappear, an exhibition of Nightsea Crossing intended to be acquired in its entirety, keeping every moment, in order to create a unique moment. This "expo-collection" was acquired in 1986 (designated by inventory number 986.4.1)

In 1995 the artists decided to donate objects that had participated in the various sittings (all designated by inventory number 995.2.1)
Title: Nightsea Crossing
Place of production: Sydney 1981; Marl 1982; Dusseldorf 1982; Berlin 1982; Cologne 1982; Amsterdam, 1982; Chicago, 1982; Toronto, May 1982; Documenta 7, Kassel, August 1982, Documenta 7, Kassel, September 1982; Helsinki, 1982; Amsterdam, April 1982; Atheneum Museum, Helsinki, October 1983; Gent, 1984; Furka (Switzerland), September 1984; Stedelijk Museum, Bonn, 1984; Middelburg, 1984; Ushimado, February 1985 (first International Biennial); Sao Paulo, 1985; New York, 1986; Lyon, 1986.
Description:
The elements acquired in 1986 are:

Two tables:

-A mahogany table and two upholstered armchairs

-A golden circular table whose tray is divided into eight parts.
In Nightsea Crossing Conjunction, which took place in April 1983 at the Fodor Museum in Amsterdam, the rectangular table was replaced by a round table, specially made for the occasion and wrapped with a gold leaf. To make the event different and exceptional, Ulay and Marina invited two other people to this "silent symposium": a llama from Tibet and a member of the Pintupi tribe from the desert of Central Australia.
Also included are four photographic prints of this stage of Nightsea Crossing.

86 cibachromes:
-Colors : 46 cibachromes
During each Nightsea Crossing session, Marina and Ulay are dressed in suit combinations of different colours according to the numbering of the Vedic square. The colours were also related to the date and location of the sitting.

-Sittings : 20 cibachromes
20 photographs of the places where the sittings were made

-Snakes : 16 cibachromes

-3 other cibachromes of certain objects used in sittings (scissors, elephant and gold)

Purpose:
-A water fountain equipped with a cup and a tap. The fountain can is filled with water mixed with gold leaf
12 golden javelots bound in beam by a scarf of black fabric
Materials, supports, techniques: Cibachrome prints framed under plexi (86), circular table without wooden foot, gilded with leaf (8 elements), golden javelets with leaf (12), fountain, gold leaf, water.
Acquisition:
Purchased at Michael Klein Gallery in 1986
with the help of FRAM Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes

Title: Nightsea Crossing
Place of production: Sydney 1981; Marl 1982; Dusseldorf 1982; Berlin 1982; Cologne 1982; Amsterdam 1982; Chicago 1982; Gent 1984; Helsinki, 1982; Middelburg, 1984; Sao Paulo, 1985; Ushimado, February 1985 (first International Biennial); Toronto, May 1982; Furka (Switzerland), September 1984; Atheneum Museum, Helsinki, October 1983; Middleburg; Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam, April 1982; Documenta 7, Kassel, August 1982, Documenta 7, Kassel, September 1982; Bonn, 1984; New York, 1986; Lyon, 1988.
Description:
In 1995, the two artists decided to transfer to the museum all the photos, objects and documents of Nightsea Crossing still in their possession and which had not been exhibited in 1986.

The authenticity of the objects is not certain. The Chinese scissors were acquired in Lyon in 1999.

-4 boomerangs
Boomerangs are installed as an inverted swastika.
Used in 1981 in Sydney, during the performance Gold Found by the Artists, which will become the first performance of Nightsea Crossing.

Chinese scissors
Marina and Ulay performed at the Kunstakademie in Düsseldorf for 3 days in March 1982.
During this sitting, a pair of Chinese scissors are planted in the mahogany table.
The Chinese scissors were acquired in Lyon in 1999.

-Paper boat
Marina and Ulay perform at Fundaçao Calouste Gulbenkian in Lisbon for two days in June 1985.
Weighing this sitting, a white boat folded in paper was placed in the center of the table.

- Cristal
Marina and Ulay performed at the Skulpturenmuseum in Marl for one day in March 1982.
During this sitting, a quartz crystal, found by the artists in the Australian desert, is placed in the center of the table.

- Elephant.
Marina and Ulay performed at the Kunsthaus Berthanien in Berlin for 3 days in March 1982.
During this sitting, an uncooked clay elephant statuette is placed in the centre of the table, attached with string tips.
Materials, supports, techniques: Quartz crystal with 6 sides, 1 white paper folding boat, pair of Chinese scissors, boomerangs, clay, wood, fabric, plywood.
Publishable comment:
"For Nightsea Crossing we made a table and two mahogany chairs, without metal nails. The dimensions of the table had this peculiarity of being based on the number three (...) This table and the two chairs will have travelled with us until the end of Nightsea Crossing (...) Sometimes we had placed symbolic objects on the table".
Statement by Marina Abramovic, page 74 of the catalogue
Marina Abramovic, Editions du Centre Pompidou, Paris, 1990.

Title: City of Angels
Description:
In Ayutthaya, a former Thai capital, characters frozen in their ancestral history appear a text, spoken and sung, that of Rama VI, king of Ayutthaya. A Buddhist monk, a Thai family, two workers, a little girl, a warrior, constitute this micro-society of a past buried in the ruins. They were filmed for five minutes in real time, without cutting, at sunset and at sunrise, each shot was made only once.
Artists describe in a series of living paintings the life and rituals of Thai Buddhism. A harmonious and meditative atmosphere, mixing religious songs and Thai faces: "a culture presented as a living being" (Ulay).
Materials, supports, techniques: Video performance copied on laser disc

Title: Becoming visible
Production circumstances:
Work produced and shown for the first time from 5 December 1992 to 11 February 1993 at the Dukes of Württemberg castle.

- Association Unit Mobile de Besançon

Description:
The videos of the installation are therefore excerpts from this Dragon Heads performance series.
These extracts are close-ups of the artist's face with a snake moving on his head.
The extracts were first reworked at the time. Action is slow motion( slow motion). The extracts are repeated in loop for a total time of 30min.
A work is also done on the soundtrack. We can hear in voice the voice of the artist. This sound was added in addition and is not present in the initial performance. Marina Abramovic scans indefinitely, at the rhythm of the movement of snakes, words relating to the different energies diffused by the human body and the crystal: "Follow the energy of my skin" (follow the energy of my skin), "Follow the crystal skin" (follow the skin of the crystal), "Follow the heat of my skin" (follow the heat of my skin), "Follow the heart", "Follow my energies".
Materials, supports, techniques: Video installation: 7 wooden tables; 28 crystals; 7 monitors; 7 video players; 1 computer; 7 videos: color, sound, monitor
Additional dimensions:
-Installation set: Variable size, Minimum diameter of 600 cm
-Table : 69.5 x 60x: 38.5c m
Height of the tray : 2 cm, Height of the body : 11,5cm, Height of the body with the tray : 13,5c m
-Monitor: 42.5 x 56.5 x 58 cm, Frame depth: 17cm
-Reader: 19 x 42.5 x 44.5c m
-Ordinator:
Screen: 33.7 x 32.5 x 32c m
Central unit: 15 x 40 x 40c m
Keyboard: 5 x 47.5 x 17.5c m
-Crystals: weight of the set:Weight of the set: about 1.2t,Weight of each crystal: 40kg
-Video: total loop duration: 30
Publishable comment:
Explanation of change of title:
"At first, this work was called Dragon Heads. This name refers in general to the performances, the seven performances that I have performed in seven different places, in the last two-three years, and where I embroider variations on the same theme. On me, on my head, there are several snakes, real snakes alive. They move slowly along my body, highlighting its energy lines while I remain completely motionless. When I imagined this installation, I wanted to combine other things too, not only performance elements but also sculptural elements, I wanted to use minerals, my own voice, which did not exist in performance. I wanted a clear connection between the earth, minerals, snakes and my body. That's why, during this process, the name title changed to finally "get visible". This relationship and this link between the various elements, which existed at the beginning at the subconscious level, become totally visible during the final process."
Marina Abramovic (from an interview with Dunja Blazevic)

Title: Shoum
Collaborators: Co-producer : Galleria SpazioA, Pistoia (Italy)
Description: Zdjelar的s video work »Shoum« starts with a blank, we see no image, but hear the sound of the 1984 Tears for Fears mega hit ‘Shout There we see an iPod, a sheet of paper and the hands of two men from Belgrade, holding thoughts. Over the race of the next seven minutes we see how the two attempt to decipher the lyrics of ‘Shout This is in fact the case, considering that these men speak no English. Thus they phonetically transcribe what they hear, based on their own vocabulary and ability to vocally interpret the unfamily. ‘Shoum Shoum Lajdi o Laus, they write and sing, in a strange invented language somewhere between phonetic transcription, Serbian, and English, as ‘Tears for Fears' sing ‘Shout, shout, let it all out We know how through error and deformations an entirely ‘new language' is being created, which intriguingly relates to the original in a shifted way, namely acoustically. As quickly comes clear, meeting here is less a matter of understanding than of processing and assimilation. Cut off from the lingua franca of a globalized world, with perseverance these two men create something of their own that lies between the foreign and the family. The work that opens up space for critique by embracing the artist Mladen Stilinovic
Materials, supports, techniques: video 16/9th ,color and stereo sound
Publishable comment: transfer of limited rights to the Seine-Saint-Denis (2030)

Lives / Works: Lives and works in Durban, South Africa
Title: San Pedro V (The Hope I hope)
Description: Tracey Rose wanders in leopard panties and princess crown, the body painted in pink and the eyes surrounded by black, at the foot of the separation wall between Israelis and Palestinians on which she ends up urinating after pulling from her electric guitar the Israeli anthem, punctuated with larsens and saturated sounds. The inscription on the wall, "Decolonize the Mind", coupled with the motif of the barrier, invites the spectator to destroy the formal, symbolic and material separations around which the relations of strength and domination are formed.
Materials, supports, techniques: DVD, 6 min
Publishable comment: At the same time brave and comic, Tracey Rose's action is meant to "make humor and provoke a reaction, to point the absurdity of the situation". (p 21 of the exhibition guide of the Biennale d'Art Contemporain de Lyon 2011, intended for the public).

Acquise at the end of the Biennale d'art contemporain de Lyon 2011

Lives / Works: Lives and works in Durban, South Africa
Title: The Black Paintings : dead White Man
Description: It is first of all the dying ultrasound coming out of the artist's throat that must be distinguished. To this is superimposed the pronunciation of the names of the dead, famous victims — political martyrs? And then the word "white" repeated until breathlessness. And the loop goes back. And what do we see? First the place of worship, painted cardboard altar, where names are repeated again. Then the priestess who enters, a pagan priestess and demon: she turns our backs, the body grey, brown, painted, muddy, ironically Adamic. Start a dance of which we do not know whether it is lamentation or exorcism. In the end, she will turn around, face us, and we will see that she carries life. This body that turned our backs is also a memory, rooted in the work of Rose, of Sawtche Baartman (see Venus Baartman, 2001), known as the Black Venus or Hottentote, with which the artist shares Khoisan origins.
Materials, supports, techniques: Video, color, sound

Title:
The Mumble of the Homecoming Oak
(The whisper of the oak)
Description:
Immersive installation in situ with branches of a fallen oak in the Rhône-Alpes region.
Sound recordings and leaf skeletons were produced as a participatory process with local residents. The branches of the tree and the leaves are animated by the sound of the participants' testimonies via the vibrations of the transducers.
Materials, supports, techniques: Wood (oak branches), oak leaf skeletons, 2 transducers, multimedia/computer player, cables, sound files, steel supports.

Title: Fruit of the Dark Womb
Description: Representations of dolls that appear to be drawn almost automatically from the hand by a sucession of fine and hachure lines, sometimes showing brightly coloured flats.
Materials, supports, techniques: paper pencil, pastel
Additional dimensions:
2 drawings: 25 x 17 cm
3 framed drawings : 146 x 98 cm
Publishable comment:
For Virginia Chihota, the doll is incapacitated: the inability to speak, react, hit or turn the blows. "You can do anything to a doll." ( V. Chihota, Exhibition Catalogue A terrible beauty is born).
She also reveals that the dolls she spontaneously designed in her notebooks were used during fertility rituals.
